title: BNCI 2015-006 Music BCI dataset
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing a multi-streamed musical oddball task designed to investigate auditory attention and brain-computer interface applications. Participants selectively attended to one of three concurrent instruments in polyphonic music clips while detecting deviant patterns, with EEG signals recorded at 64 channels and preprocessed for P300 classification. The study demonstrates that attended instruments in complex musical stimuli can be reliably decoded from ongoing EEG activity with 91% accuracy, establishing polyphonic music as a novel and ecologically valid stimulus modality for auditory BCI research.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 64 active electrodes (10-10 montage, Brain Products actiCAP) at 1000 Hz with left mastoid reference. Participants listened to 40-second polyphonic music clips containing three concurrent instruments (Synth-Pop or Jazz conditions) with embedded standard and deviant patterns. Participants were cued to attend to one instrument and count deviants. Data were downsampled to 250 Hz, lowpass filtered (Chebyshev, 42 Hz passband), epoched from -200 to 1200 ms, baseline corrected, and artifact rejected using min-max criterion (100 μV threshold on Fp1/Fp2). Classification employed LDA with shrinkage covariance on spatio-temporal features using leave-one-clip-out cross-validation.
